overview.description: Baseball is a thematic 7-Card Stud poker variant where 3s and 9s are wild, and 4s earn players extra cards. It is primarily played as a high-action 'Dealer's Choice' game in North American home poker circles. For the full technical specification, mechanical rules, and engine data, please see the master entry for Baseball Poker.

history.origins: Originating in mid-20th century America, Baseball capitalized on the popularity of 7-Card Stud and the national obsession with the sport. It became a staple of 'social' poker where the goal was to create massive, wild hands that would be impossible in formal casino play.
timeline: 1950s: Rules for wild 3s and 9s appear in regional US Hoyle editions.
1970s: The 'Match the Pot' penalty is standardized in many home game variations.
Present: Remains a favorite 'chaos' game in mixed-game poker rotations.
history.evolution: The game's rules (3 strikes, 9 innings, 4 balls) are a direct mapping of baseball terminology to card ranks.
history.cultural: A cultural icon of the 'Poker in the Den' era of American social life.

setup.players: Two to six players. Because face-up fours grant extra cards, more than six players risks running out of deck; the game is therefore capped at six.

rules.objective: Win the pot with the best 5-card hand using 3s and 9s as wild cards.
rules.gameplay: 7-card stud: two down, four up, one down. 3s and 9s wild; 4s grant extra card; face-up 3 requires match pot or fold. Best five-card hand wins pot.
keyRules: A 4 dealt face up grants the player an extra card immediately.
A 3 dealt face up requires the player to match the current pot or fold.

strategy.basic: Focus on collecting wild cards (3s and 9s). A 'natural' hand like a Straight is often useless against the high-powered hands of this variant.
strategy.intermediate: Manage pot exposure when you have a face-up 3; decide when to match the pot or fold. Use position and visible wilds to size bets.
strategy.advanced: Read opponents' possible hands from their upcards and the number of live 3s and 9s; balance bluffing with value when wilds are scarce.
tips: Keep track of the number of wild cards already showing on the board.
Be prepared for large pots due to the 'match the pot' 3 rule.

list.name: Face-up 3 match pot
list.description: A player who is dealt a three face up must immediately either match the pot or fold, or pay a fixed amount to the pot.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes the betting penalty when a face-up three appears; the underlying stud dealing engine stays the same.

list.name: Face-down 4s extra card
list.description: Some play that concealed fours also grant an extra card when revealed; timing of reveal varies by house rules.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This variant changes when extra cards for concealed fours are claimed, which is handled in rules text rather than separate engine overrides.

list.name: Football
list.description: Threes and sixes are wild; a two grants the player an extra card.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Football keeps the same stud structure as Baseball but swaps which ranks are wild and which grant extra cards.

list.name: Woolworth
list.description: Fives and tens are wild; some play that a two grants an extra card.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Woolworth changes the special ranks and payments while leaving the base seven-card stud dealing pattern unchanged.

difficulty.easy: Easy Baseball Poker opponents play straightforwardly, overvalue natural hands, and seldom raise aggressively unless showing very strong upcards.
difficulty.medium: Medium Baseball Poker opponents track visible threes, nines, and fours, manage pot size around match-the-pot situations, and mix in occasional semi-bluffs.
difficulty.hard: Hard Baseball Poker opponents reason from upcards and betting patterns to estimate hand strength, aggressively leverage wild cards, and adjust pressure based on pot size and position.

considerations: AI should account for the density of wild threes and nines when deciding whether a natural-looking hand is likely to be best.
AI should treat face-up fours as both strength and volatility, since extra cards can create very strong but also very obvious hands.

reveal_market.reason: Baseball is a stud poker variant where all cards are dealt directly to players; no market exists.

buy_market.reason: Cards cannot be purchased from a market in this game; extra cards are awarded only by rule triggers.

buy_stock.reason: Players receive their cards through fixed dealing rounds rather than through a stock purchase mechanic.

fold.description: Forfeit hand and any claim to pot.
fold.constraints: When not matching pot on face-up 3.

check.description: Bet zero when no bet to call.

call.description: Match current bet to stay in.

declare.reason: Hand resolution occurs automatically during the showdown comparison rather than through a declaration.

play_card.reason: This is a hand-ranking game where cards are received and held rather than played to a shared trick.

draw.reason: Extra cards are awarded automatically by the four-up rule and are not handled by a general draw action.

discard.reason: Players must retain all cards dealt to them to form the best five-card poker combination at showdown.

pass.reason: A turn cannot be skipped without taking a wagering action (check, bet, or fold) during the round.

bid.reason: Baseball Poker uses standard poker wagering rounds rather than an auction-style bidding system.

meld.reason: The game focuses on five-card poker hand rankings rather than the creation of melds or sequences.

go_out.reason: The deal terminates only after the final betting round and the subsequent showdown have been completed.

edgeCases.text: A four dealt face up grants the player one extra face-up card immediately before the next player receives a card; players with fours may have eight or more cards at showdown.
Some play that a face-up three requires the player to match the current pot or fold (or pay a fixed amount to the pot).
Each betting round is begun by the player with the highest hand showing at that time.
Five betting rounds: one after each round of face-up cards and one after the final card.
Five of a kind is the highest hand type when using wild cards.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck of four French suits with thirteen ranks ace through two; no jokers. Used for Baseball Poker, a seven-card stud variant where threes and nines are wild and fours grant extra cards.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), standard for poker. Suit identity matters only for flush and same-suit hand evaluation in this stud variant.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit (ace through two). In Baseball Poker threes and nines are wild; fours dealt face up grant the player an extra card. Standard poker rank order applies for hand comparison.
engine.dealPattern: 2 down, 4 up, 1 down (seven-card stud); face-up four grants one extra card before next player receives a card.

hero.title: BASEBALL
hero.subtitle: 7-Card Stud Wild
hero.tagline: Threes and nines wild; fours deal extra. Match the pot or fold.

synthesis.shortDescription: Thematic stud variant with 3s and 9s wild and 4s granting extra cards. Best five-card hand wins the pot.

scoring.description: Standard poker hand ranking. Pot goes to best five-card hand at showdown.
scoring.winCondition: Best five-card hand wins the pot.

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target; play continues for as many deals as the players agree or until one player has all of the chips.
nullReasons.scoringDirection: High hand wins the pot; there is no cumulative score track where points go up or down between deals.
nullReasons.cardValues: Baseball Poker resolves each pot using standard poker hand rankings with wild cards; individual per-rank point values are not tracked.
